item.title: Round money only via round_money
item.content: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.

item.title: Money operations need keyword-only idempotency_key
item.content: Every operation that moves money or mutates a payment/credit must accept a keyword-only `idempotency_key`; check `ledgerly.audit.events()` for an existing entry with that key and return early, and pass `idempotency_key` into `audit.record`.

review_comments: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment/credit must accept a keyword-only `idempotency_key`. If an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return without applying the operation again, and include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.

[team convention] Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 need a second approver (finance policy FIN-2026-03): accept a keyword-only `approved_by` and raise BillingError("approval_required") when it is missing for amounts above the threshold.

evidence.quote: Every operation that moves money or changes a payment/credit must accept a keyword-only `idempotency_key`.

item.title: Raise BillingError with code and detail
item.content: Signal invalid input by raising `ledgerly.errors.BillingError(code, detail)` with a snake_case code string, e.g. `BillingError("invalid_tax_rate", str(rate_percent))`.

item.title: Parse rates via Decimal(str(...))
item.content: When a numeric argument may be a float, parse it with `Decimal(str(value))` and catch `InvalidOperation`/`ValueError` rather than passing it to `to_money`, which rejects floats.
